title: Why demons must not be served
source_text: Φαύλους δὲ δαίμονας οὐ μόνοι λέγομεν ἡμεῖς ἀλλὰ καὶ σχεδὸν πάντες. ὅσοι δαίμονας τιθέασιν εἶναι. οὐ πάντα οὖν ἔχει νόμον ἐκ τοῦ μεγίστου θεοῦ. ὅσα γὰρ παρ᾿ ἰδίαν ἀπροσεξίαν, κακίαν ἢ πονηρίαν ἢ ἄγνοιαν τῶν καλῶν, ἀποπέπτωκε τοῦ θείου νόμου, οὐκ ἔχει τὸν νόμον τοῦ θεοῦ ἀλλ᾿, ἵνα ὀνομάσω καινῷ ὀνόματι καὶ τῷ κατὰ τὴν γραφὴν, τὸν νόμον ἔχει „τῆς ἁμαρτίας.“ κατὰ μὲν οὖν τοὺς πολλοὺς τῶν τιθέντων εἶναι δαίμονας καὶ οἱ φαῦλοι δαίμονες οὐκ ἔχουσι τὸν ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ νόμον ἀλλὰ παρανομοῦσι· κατὰ δὲ ἡμᾶς πάντες δαίμονες ἀποπεσόντες τῆς ἐπὶ τὸ ἀγαθὸν ὁδοῦ, πρότερον οὐκ ὄντες δαίμονες· καὶ ἔστιν εἶδος τῶν ἐκπεσόντων θεοῦ τὸ τῶν δαιμόνων. διόπερ οὐ χρὴ θεραπεύειν δαίμονας ὅστις σέβει θεόν. δηλοῦται δὲ τὰ περὶ τοὺς δαίμονας καὶ ἐκ τῶν καλούντων δαίμονας ἐπὶ τοῖς ὀνομαζομένοις φίλτροις ἢ μισήθροις ἢ ἐπὶ κωλύσεσι πράξεων ἢ ἄλλων τοιούτων μυρίων· ἅπερ ποιοῦσιν οἱ δι᾿ ἐπῳδῶν καὶ μαγγανειῶν μεμαθηκότες καλεῖν καὶ ἐπάγεσθαι δαίμονας ἐφ᾿ ἃ βούλονται. διόπερ ἡ πάντων δαιμόνων θεραπεία ἀλλοτρία ἡμῶν ἐστι, τῶν σεβόντων τὸν ἐπὶ πᾶσι θεόν. καὶ θεραπεία δαιμόνων ἐστὶν ἡ θεραπεία τῶν νομιζομένων θεῶν· „πάντες“ γὰρ „οἱ θεοὶ τῶν ἐθνῶν δαιμόνια.“ δῆλον δὲ καὶ τοῦτο ἐκ τοῦ εἰς τὰ δοκοῦντα ἐνεργέστερα τῶν νομιζομένων ἱερῶν κατακλίσεις περιέργους γεγονέναι καὶ κατὰ τὰς ἀρχὰς τῆς ἱδρύσεως τῶν τοιῶνδε ξοάνων καὶ νεῶν, ἅστινας κατακλίσεις οἱ τῇ τῶν δαιμόνων διὰ μαγγανειῶν θεραπείᾳ σχολάζοντες πεποίηνται. διὸ δέδοκται ἡμῖν φεύγειν ὡς ὄλεθρον τὴν τῶν δαιμόνων θεραπείαν· δαιμόνων δὲ θεραπείαν εἶναί φαμεν πᾶσαν τὴν νομιζομένην παρ᾿ Ἕλλησι παρὰ βωμοῖς καὶ ἀγάλμασι καὶ ναοῖς θεῶν θρησκείαν.
pass_a_gloss: And base/wicked (φαῦλοι) demons not we alone speak of, but also almost all, as many as posit (τίθημι) demons to exist. Not all things then have a law from the greatest God. For as many things as by their own inattention/heedlessness (ἀπροσεξία), vice (κακία) or wickedness (πονηρία) or ignorance (ἄγνοια) of the good things (τὰ καλά), have fallen away (ἀποπίπτω) from the divine law, do not have the law of God but, that I may name it with a new (καινός) name and the one according to the writing/Scripture (γραφή), have the law 'of sin (ἁμαρτία)'. According then to the many of those positing demons to exist, also the base demons do not have the law from God but transgress (παρανομέω); but according to us all demons [are] having fallen away from the road (ὁδός) toward the good (τὸ ἀγαθόν), formerly not being demons; and the kind (εἶδος) of demons is [one] of those fallen out (ἐκπίπτω) from God. Therefore (διόπερ) it is not necessary to serve demons, whoever reveres God. And the things about demons are made clear (δηλόω) also from those calling (καλέω) demons for the so-called (ὀνομαζόμενα) love-charms (φίλτρα) or hate-charms (μίσηθρα) or for hindrances (κωλύσεις) of actions (πράξεις) or ten thousand (μυρία) others such; which those do who through incantations (ἐπῳδαί) and sorceries (μαγγανεῖαι) have learned (μανθάνω) to call and bring on (ἐπάγομαι) demons for what they wish. Therefore the service (θεραπεία) of all demons is foreign (ἀλλοτρία) to us, those revering the God over all. And the service of the supposed (νομιζόμενοι) gods is service of demons; for 'all the gods of the nations [are] demons (δαιμόνια)'. And this too is clear from elaborate/magical (περίεργοι) installations/settings-down (κατακλίσεις) having taken place into the seemingly more effective (ἐνεργέστερα) of the supposed sanctuaries (ἱερά), also at the beginnings of the founding (ἵδρυσις) of such wooden images (ξόανα) and temples, which installations those occupied (σχολάζω) with the service of demons through sorceries have made. Therefore it has been resolved (δοκέω) by us to flee (φεύγω) as ruin/destruction (ὄλεθρος) the service of demons; and we say all the religion/worship (θρησκεία) of gods customary (νομίζομαι) among Greeks at altars and images and temples to be service of demons.
pass_b_english: We are not the only ones to speak of wicked demons; nearly all who hold that demons exist do so. Not everything, then, has a law from the greatest God. For whatever has fallen away from the divine law, through its own heedlessness, vice or wickedness, or ignorance of what is good, does not have the law of God; rather, to use a new name, the one found in Scripture, it has the law “of sin” (Romans 7:23; 8:2). According to most of those who hold that demons exist, then, the wicked demons do not have the law that comes from God, but transgress it. According to us, however, all demons have fallen away from the road that leads to the good, and were not demons before; and the demons are one kind among those who have fallen away from God. Therefore whoever worships God must not serve demons.

The truth about demons is made plain also by those who summon demons for what are called love-charms or hate-charms, or to hinder undertakings, or for countless other such purposes. This is done by those who have learned through incantations and sorceries to summon demons and draw them to whatever they wish. Therefore the service of all demons is foreign to us, who worship the God over all. And the service of the reputed gods is service of demons, for “all the gods of the nations are demons” (Psalm 96:5). This is plain also from the fact that, at the very founding of such wooden images and temples, magical rites of installation were performed in those of the so-called sanctuaries that are thought more potent; and these rites were performed by those who devote themselves to the service of demons through sorcery. For this reason we have resolved to flee from the service of demons as from destruction; and we say that all the worship of gods practised among the Greeks at altars, images and temples is service of demons.

choices.choice: ‘The law of sin’: Paul’s phrase in Romans 7:23 (‘the law of sin which is in my members’; also 7:25) and Romans 8:2 (‘the law of sin and death’); Origen calls it a ‘new name ... according to Scripture’. ‘All the gods of the nations are demons’ is Psalm 95:5 LXX, English numbering Psalm 96:5 (Hebrew text: ‘idols’). ‘Whoever worships God must not serve demons’ repeats Celsus’s report of Christian teaching (7.62, 7.67), now affirmed by Origen in his own voice; no quotation marks, since Origen speaks for himself here. ἀπροσεξίαν, κακίαν ἢ πονηρίαν: the comma follows the staged text; rendered ‘heedlessness, vice or wickedness’. κατακλίσεις περιέργους: περίεργος often means ‘magical’ (as τὰ περίεργα in Acts 19:19); κατάκλισις is the rite that settles a power in an image or shrine (compare κατακλιθέντες in 7.64); rendered ‘magical rites of installation’ (one word for περιέργους, not two). ξόανα: wooden cult images. κωλύσεσι πράξεων: ‘to hinder undertakings’ (spells binding another person’s actions).
'elaborate magic rites of installation' -> 'magical rites of installation' (περιέργους rendered once, not twice); note updated
Romans 7:23; 8:2 ('law of sin') and Psalm 96:5 (LXX 95:5, 'demons') confirmed
